title: GraphQL Queries
description: Master the art of querying data with GraphQL

questions.explanation: A GraphQL query is a request to read data from the server, specifying exactly which fields you need.
acceptable_answers: a way to fetch specific fields
questions.hint: It's the GraphQL equivalent of HTTP GET

questions.text: How do you ask for specific fields in a GraphQL query?
questions.explanation: You list the field names inside curly braces, e.g., { user { name email } }
acceptable_answers: specify them in the query body

questions.text: What is query nesting in GraphQL?
questions.explanation: Query nesting allows you to request related data in a single query by following relationships, e.g., user { posts { title } }
questions.hint: It's about getting related data without multiple requests

questions.text: What are query variables and why are they useful?
questions.explanation: Query variables allow you to parameterize queries, making them reusable and enabling dynamic values.

questions.text: What is query aliasing in GraphQL?
questions.explanation: Aliasing allows you to request the same field multiple times with different names, e.g., { current: user { name } past: user { id } }
acceptable_answers: requesting same field with different names
questions.hint: It's about requesting the same thing but calling it something else
